scenes.heading: Tungsten Engine
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Tungsten Engine and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What Tungsten optimizes
items: Memory management off the JVM heap
scenes.narration: Tungsten is Spark's execution backend, focused on squeezing maximum performance out of modern CPUs and memory. It manages memory in a compact binary format, often off the JVM heap, to slash garbage-collection pressure. It also lays data out to be cache-friendly and generates specialized bytecode for entire stages.

scenes.heading: Row objects vs Tungsten binary
scenes.narration: Traditional JVM row objects carry heavy per-object headers and scatter data across the heap, which triggers frequent garbage collection and cache misses. Tungsten instead stores rows as compact binary records in contiguous memory, often off-heap, so the CPU reads them sequentially. This eliminates most GC work and keeps hot data close to the processor caches.

scenes.heading: Whole-stage codegen
scenes.narration: A signature Tungsten feature is whole-stage code generation. Instead of calling a chain of operator objects per row, Spark fuses all the operators in a stage into a single generated Java function. That function is compiled at runtime and iterates over rows in a tight loop with no virtual calls. The effect is code that runs close to what a hand-written program would achieve.

scenes.code:
df = spark.range(0, 100_000_000)
res = df.selectExpr("id * 2 as x").filter("x % 4 == 0")
res.explain()
# Look for '*(1)' markers = WholeStageCodegen is active
scenes.heading: Spotting codegen in the plan
scenes.narration: When you call explain on a query, operators wrapped in a WholeStageCodegen boundary appear with an asterisk and a stage number. That marker tells you Spark fused those operators into one compiled function. If an operator lacks the asterisk, it fell back to the slower interpreted path, which is a useful signal when tuning.

scenes.text: Tungsten makes Spark CPU-efficient, not just distributed.
scenes.narration: Prefer built-in expressions over Python UDFs so your logic stays inside Tungsten's generated code. Stepping outside it forces slow row-by-row serialization.
